payload.text:
No Utilz-tree file contains the popupart theme; it arrives over SHOWREEL_THEME_PATH and a build resolving it warns that it came from off the built-ins.
AUDITED 2026-09-09 17:38Z BY vc. TWO LEGS VERIFIED AND DRIVEN, ONE HALF-BUILT, SO THE ROW STAYS UNSATISFIED. LEG 1 -- THE THEME'S SUBSTANCE IS ABSENT AND THE WORDING IS CORRECTED TO SAY WHAT WAS MEASURED. Measured across the whole tracked tree: ZERO .woff2 files, ZERO favicon files, and no popupart theme.css -- the only shipped theme is crates/showreel/themes/default/theme.css. So popupart cannot be rendered from this tree, which is the property. THE ABSOLUTE WORDING WAS FALSE, THOUGH, AND A FALSE ROW IS WORSE THAN AN OPEN ONE: crates/showreel/fixtures/popupart.theme.yaml is a Utilz-tree file that contains popupart's theme MANIFEST, and cc's phrase "a manifest, not a theme" understates it -- the manifest carries the brand description "POP^UP^ART by Snorkeltoast. Comic four-up palette, keyline black.", the token source path, and five font FAMILY names. That is the theme's identity without its bytes. The exemption is stated and MEASURED rather than argued: the fixture is #[cfg(test)] and does not reach the release binary. Driven by vc independently of cc and over a wider token set -- popupart, POP^UP^ART, Snorkeltoast, "Luckiest Guy", "keyline black" and "Ash Sinclair" all return ZERO from `strings` on target/release/showreel, WITH A CONTROL PROVING THE INSTRUMENT WORKS ON THAT BINARY: showreel 11, theme.yaml 4, woff2 2. cc measured the first three tokens; the last three are vc's, and the brand DESCRIPTION and a font family were the ones worth adding because they are what a manifest carries and a name does not. LEG 2 -- DRIVEN, BOTH DIRECTIONS, BOTH INVOCATION FORMS. Without SHOWREEL_THEME_PATH both `prez showreel check` and `utilz prez showreel check` exit 2 with "no theme 'popupart'", stating that the variable is unset and NO directories were searched, listing the one built-in, and naming three remedies. With it, both exit 0 and resolve to the path. LEG 3 IS HALF-BUILT AND THAT IS WHY THE ROW IS NOT SATISFIED. The row says a BUILD resolving it warns, and there is no build verb yet. The WARNING ITSELF EXISTS, is driven, and is better than the row asked: "theme 'popupart' came from <dir> (on SHOWREEL_THEME_PATH), not from the built-ins. Elsewhere this reel refuses to build until that directory is on the path." The second sentence names the consequence on a DIFFERENT machine, which is exactly the H1 trap cc flagged separately, so the warning pre-empts the confusion rather than merely reporting provenance. It fires at theme RESOLUTION, which build will share -- but sharing a mechanism is not the same as the verb existing, and this contract has already paid once for grading a two-leg row on the leg that was built. DISCHARGED WHEN `prez showreel build` exists and the same warning is driven through it.
